items.summary: CUDA 13.4 introduces a new time-sharing mode that enforces an exact memory boundary per workload, transparent to the application and alongside existing sm-sharing compute sharing in MPS. Because GPUs cannot be fractioned alone, NVIDIA released gpu-fractioning, an open-source Kubernetes operator hosted under the KAI Scheduler organization on GitHub, which runs next to the GPU Operator to supervise daemons, apply pod memory limits and compute modes before startup, and report per-fraction usage. The first integrated scheduler is KAI Scheduler v0.18.0's NvFractions mode; any scheduler that writes the required annotations can enforce fractions. Workloads request capacity via absolute sizes or GPU portions with optional burst limits, choosing between serial time-slicing (default) and parallel SM-sharing across one error domain each. Installation uses a helm upgrade command, which also installs gpu-fractioning as a dependency, enabling fractional workloads described through pod annotations at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah, Nov. 9-12.
items.title: NVIDIA CUDA 13.4 Adds Memory-Enforced GPU Sharing for Kubernetes

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission published Anthropic’s S-1 form on Monday ahead of its initial public offering, drawing attention to the company’s ballooning revenues versus higher costs. Across 93 pages and over 70,000 words, the Risk Factors section lists hundreds of potential problems. The publication notes some risks are existential: near-future models that could “accelerate[s] AI progress beyond our ability to evaluate and safeguard new model,” Anthropic warns.
items.title: Anthropic’s IPO filing surfaces existential-AI risk warnings

items.summary: AI company Anthropic and CEO Dario Amodei have repeatedly claimed their models will revolutionize biology, but the company's Monday IPO filing struck a humbler tone. It acknowledged limited experience with physical experimentation and drug development challenges. While still touting AI's potential to accelerate progress, the filing noted discoveries must pass lengthy testing and may never generate revenue.
items.title: Anthropic Softens Biology Ambitions in IPO Filing

items.summary: As Anthropic nears its IPO, the article explains how its corporate structure limits public-market investors’ control. A public benefit company status protects board decisions on AI safety from shareholder lawsuits. The founders hold 50.1% of voting power to elect three directors, while a Long-Term Benefit Trust can elect and remove a majority of the board. Employees may overrule LTBT nominations for Specified directors. Founders’ control ends ten years after the IPO or when fewer than three remain; the trust then continues until 85% of common shareholders vote to end it.
items.title: Anthropic’s layered governance keeps common shareholders out

items.summary: Prabha Jha, a Verizon leader, enrolled in MIT xPRO’s AI for Senior Executives program and co-wrote The AI Anthology with 20 other leaders. She estimates that “30 percent of what I was learning was from the program, material, and professor” while “70 percent was my peers and the interactions.” Originally set to graduate two months early, a hospital stay delayed her completion; she then joined the next cohort for another five days with 100 brand-new peers. The experience strengthened her AI skills and relationships, which she is now applying to support small and medium-sized businesses navigating AI implementation.
items.title: Verizon Leader Co-Authoring AI Insights Book After MIT Program

items.summary: US stocks closed up on Oct 27 as an anticipated Anthropic IPO lifted chip shares for a third straight session amid strong Q3 reporting, with 83% of S&P 500 reporters beating expectations per LSEG. The Nasdaq led gains while the Philadelphia Semiconductor index outperformed despite sitting more than 20% below its June record high. Meta raised US$97.5 billion (S$125 billion) in its largest equity offering, pushing shares lower.
items.title: Wall Street closes higher on renewed AI optimism

items.summary: Liquid AI introduces LFM3, a family of Liquid Foundation Models built on one shared backbone across text, vision, audio, omni and decision tasks in the 2B parameter range. Each model fine-tunes on a single GPU and deploys where an application runs. LFM3-1.7B uses 35% fewer parameters than its predecessor while matching it on short prompts; with 8K tokens in context it is about 25% faster, per Liquid AI.
items.title: Liquid AI launches LFM3 for specialized multimodal models

items.summary: Ai2 released Old Ideas, Novel Problems, a study of how reliably large language models judge the novelty of scientific research ideas. The team built two pools from ICLR 2026 peer reviews—one high-novelty (154 human-authored), one lower-novelty (145 rejected)—and tested six LLM judges across prompt, reasoning budget, and formatting changes. Small prompt edits shifted accuracy by more than 50 percentage points on AI-generated ideas versus about seven points on human ones; a simple Claude Opus 4.6 baseline scored 0.854 macro-F1 at $2.59, outperforming costlier purpose-built systems (Idea Novelty Checker: 0.642 at $30.66). The authors conclude novelty evaluation remains an open problem and offer tools for further study.
items.title: Ai2 Releases Benchmark Questioning Whether LLMs Can Judge Research Novelty

items.summary: This blog introduces Databricks Lakehouse Federation, a feature that lets organizations query sensitive on-premises data and cloud-based third-party datasets together without copying or moving information. It explains how federated connections to databases like SQL Server and PostgreSQL keep first-party data in place while marketplace shares—illustrated with FactSet financial data—are joined through Unity Catalog using standard SQL. The article walks through building an investment analytics solution for a wealth management firm, where queries re-federate live sources on each run without pipelines or persisted objects. A Genie agent is described as translating natural language into the same queries. Databricks frames this approach as changing hybrid data economics by bringing compute to data rather than migrating it.
items.title: Databricks Lakehouse Federation Enables Cloud-Connected Analytics Without Data Migration

items.summary: An academic commentary argues that holding AI-related risk is becoming unavoidable for most investors, prompted by Anthropic's expected November US$2 trillion Wall Street listing. The author notes that an S&P 500 index fund exposes holders to about 44 per cent portfolio dependence on AI performance, and that six companies delivered 57 per cent of the index's gains since April. AI firms are also the largest bond borrowers, having issued about US$466 billion this year. Beyond financial exposure, Anthropic's own prospectus dedicates nearly 30 per cent to risk factors, including warnings of catastrophic or existential risks to humanity. The author concludes that global AI risks require both government regulation and private-sector participation.
items.title: Anthropic's record IPO underscores unavoidable AI risk

items.summary: Amazon published a revised software development engineer role guideline discouraging 'tokenmaxxing,' the reliance on AI tools without reviewing output, according to CNBC. The memo calls token consumption and adoption indicators 'deeply flawed' measures of AI use, warning they can raise spending and add complexity. Amazon said metrics may still factor in with care and judgment alongside other data.
items.title: Amazon warns against chasing AI usage metrics in role guideline

items.summary: At its Oracle AI World event in Las Vegas on Monday, Oracle $ORCL introduced three agentic applications designed to automate supply chain planning and procurement. The company said the tools handle supply planning allocation, shipment load planning, and procurement spend analysis.
items.title: Oracle Unveils Three Agentic Applications for Supply Chain Operations

items.summary: Tech Today reports that Apple's new iPhone Duo has sparked excitement among buyers in India, prompting a ground report from the Apple Store there. The segment asks what customers really expect from the device and what makes it appealing, covering reactions to its design and expectations for the newest product.
items.title: Apple Buyers Share Excitement Over New iPhone Duo Design and Expectations

items.summary: In this Tech Today edition, host Cyrus breaks down the anatomy of festive digital shopping fraud. India's financial cyber fraud reporting system handled over 32.80 lakh complaints and saved more than ₹11,158 crore during the season. Scammers now run cloned e-commerce portals, fake WhatsApp reward programs, and deceptive parcel delivery links demanding fee updates to siphon bank accounts. The show also compares the screenless Google Fitbit Air against the Apple Watch Ultra 4.
items.title: Tech Today unpacks festive online scams and compares two smartwatches

items.summary: NT Health has revised its account of a privacy breach at Royal Darwin Hospital, admitting that 12 patients were affected rather than the five it had earlier stated. The exposure resulted from confidential medical information being posted to Instagram by Neda Mogharehabed, an overseas-trained doctor visiting the hospital in mid-October; content reached about 28,000 followers and included patient names, ID numbers and conditions. After ABC journalists contacted affected women who said they had not been informed, NT Health acknowledged identifying seven additional patients and began contacting them to apologise and offer support. Dr Mogharehabed could not confirm how the images were posted but said she took privacy seriously.
items.title: NT Health Admits Wider Patient Impact After Instagram Privacy Breach

items.summary: The Federal Communications Commission approved Tuesday a $11.5 billion deal for Amazon Leo's acquisition of Globalstar, its satellite arm aiming to build a network competing with SpaceX Starlink. Amazon plans commercial services by end of 2026 and will acquire Apple's stake, which accounted for about 63% of Globalstar revenue last year. FCC Chair Brendan Carr said the move would increase competition in direct-to-device broadband.
items.title: FCC Approves Amazon-Globalstar Deal Challenging Starlink

items.summary: Tata Capital managing director and chief executive Rajiv Sabharwal said the Reserve Bank of India’s proposed restrictions on revolving credit for non-banking finance companies would affect only 3-4 per cent of its assets under management. Tata Capital reported a 51 per cent year-on-year jump in Q2FY27 net profit to ₹1,660 crore and loan book growth past ₹3 lakh crore.
items.title: Tata Capital CEO Downplays RBI Revolving Credit Impact

items.summary: Union cabinet secretary T V Somanathan presented a humorous but pointed classification of 12 types of secretaries at a performance review meeting in New Delhi on Tuesday. He urged the finance and commerce ministries to send their views promptly to avoid delays, noting that officers’ performance scores often cluster close to 10 on a scale of 1 to 10, leaving little room to distinguish stars from merely satisfactory performers.
items.title: Cabinet Secretary Classifies Secretaries and Urges Faster Consultations

items.summary: The New York Stock Exchange plans to launch binary return options within days, initially covering 12 securities including Apple, Nvidia and Tesla. These contracts pay $1 or nothing at expiration based on whether the underlying security crosses a strike level. Kevin Tyrrell of NYSE cited strong growth in US options markets driving this expansion into event-based trading products.
items.title: NYSE Prepares Binary Options Trading Amid Event-Driven Demand Surge
